ApiBaseUrl.Name: API Base URL
ApiBaseUrl.Hint: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API. The guided AI Provider Setup supplies presets for DeepSeek, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, and LM Studio.

ApiKey.Name: API Key
ApiKey.Hint: API key for the current API Base URL. It stays in this browser and is never synced to the world or other users. Manage it through AI Provider Setup, which masks the value and authorizes it only for the displayed endpoint. Leave blank for a keyless local server such as Ollama or LM Studio.

JevApiKey.Name: Jev API Key
JevApiKey.Hint: OpenRouter or TypeSafe AI key used only for Jev fast picks. Stored in this browser; manage it through AI Provider Setup.

JevTypeSafeEndpoint.Name: Jev TypeSafe Endpoint
JevTypeSafeEndpoint.Hint: Where a TypeSafe AI Jev key is sent: blank for api.typesafe.ai, or the address of your own CORS proxy. Manage it through AI Provider Setup.

JevSource.Name: Jev Source
JevSource.Hint: Where the separate Jev key is sent: OpenRouter or TypeSafe AI. Manage it through AI Provider Setup.

Model.Name: Model
Model.Hint: Model identifier, e.g. deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, gpt-6-luna, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash on OpenRouter, or any model your provider offers.

Temperature.Name: Creativity (temperature)
Temperature.Hint: Higher values give more creative (and less predictable) concepts. Grounding and selection operations always use temperature 0 for reliable local-model output.

MaxTokens.Name: Max response tokens
MaxTokens.Hint: Global upper limit for AI responses. Each operation applies a smaller production-safe cap where possible; reasoning is disabled so the allowance is reserved for complete structured output.

RequestTimeout.Name: Request timeout (seconds)
RequestTimeout.Hint: Abort a generation if the AI provider sends no data for this long. Responses are streamed, so slow models keep working as long as data keeps arriving — this only catches genuinely stalled connections.

RunTokenBudget.Name: Run token budget
RunTokenBudget.Hint: A run stops once it spends this many tokens across all its AI calls (default 60000). Raise it or set 0 to disable; reached limit stops the run instead of retrying forever.

RunDeadline.Name: Run deadline (minutes)
RunDeadline.Hint: Minutes before a run times out (default 5). Set 0 to turn the limit off.

FreeArchetype.Name: Free Archetype variant rule
FreeArchetype.Hint: When enabled, one-click characters gain the variant's extra archetype feat slot at each even level. Picks are validated staged — candidate-time prerequisite filtering plus slot-placement checks — and unprovable placements are left unresolved instead of guessed.

WhatsNew.Title: What's new in SimplySF2e
WhatsNew.MenuHint: See the latest changes to SimplySF2e. It also opens once by itself after an update that changes something you can see.
WhatsNew.Intro: SimplySF2e {version}: here is what changed since you last looked.
WhatsNew.IntroAll: Everything that has changed, newest first.
WhatsNew.BrokeBody: Use Copy bug report in the Generator's error box and send it, with a line on what you were doing, to whoever gave you the module.

OneScreenWelcome.Title: Set up in one screen
OneScreenWelcome.Body: The Welcome window now connects your AI in one step: pick a provider, paste your key and press Connect. It loads the model list, tests the model and offers a sample monster. A failed connect leaves your previous setup untouched.

RelevelAbilities.Title: Re-leveled creatures keep their numbers in step
RelevelAbilities.Body: When you re-level a copy, the area blasts, auras and filled glossary abilities the module built are rebuilt for the new level. Published abilities keep their text.

Aura.Title: Auras with real numbers
Aura.Body: Creatures can now have auras that call for a save and apply a condition, or deal damage each turn. The radius, save DC, condition value and damage come from GM Core and the creature's level. The aura shows on the canvas; you apply the result.

AreaBlast.Title: Breaths and blasts with real numbers
AreaBlast.Body: Creatures' breath weapons and blasts can now be working abilities. The area, damage and DC come from GM Core for the creature's level, and a limited blast can be recharged.

BlankAbilities.Title: Creature abilities get real values again
BlankAbilities.Body: Constrict, Greater Constrict, Swallow Whole, Engulf, Trample, Frightful Presence and Stench now get their damage, DCs, sizes and aura sizes for the creature's level, from the GM Core tables and published creatures. Trample uses the creature's own strike. An ability that cannot be filled, such as a tiny creature with Swallow Whole, is left out, and the console names it.

ClearerErrors.Title: Clearer error messages and bug reports
ClearerErrors.Body: Error messages now say what went wrong and what to do next. After you copy a bug report, an Open GitHub issue button takes you straight to the issue form, and the report is never put in the link.

RunDeadline.Title: Runs stop after 5 minutes
RunDeadline.Body: Runs now stop after 5 minutes by default, so a stuck request cannot hang the Generator. Change the limit, or turn it off with 0, in Module Settings: SimplySF2e, Run deadline (minutes).

RunCost.Title: Run cost
RunCost.Body: The token report now shows what a run cost when your provider reports it (OpenRouter does). For other providers, enter optional per-1M-token prices on the connection in AI Provider Setup for an estimate marked with ≈.

RunBudget.Title: Per-run token budget
RunBudget.Body: A run now stops at a token budget (60,000 by default) instead of retrying forever. The limit is a world setting.

ProviderRetry.Title: More resilient provider requests
ProviderRetry.Body: When the AI provider reports a rate limit or a transient server error, SimplySF2e can wait (honoring the provider's Retry-After when given) and try the request once. Ambiguous server errors that may already have been billed are not retried. Cancelling stops the retry.

Multiclass.Title: Multiclass, Tech Core ancestries and more
Multiclass.Body: With Free Archetype on, a player character can take a second class: pick it in the new Multiclass field or let the AI choose from your prompt. The dedication goes in the first archetype slot, and later slots favor its feats. Mystic, Witchwarper and Technomancer dedications get their own spell list. A Technomancer now has a full spell database. Living Hologram and SRO characters get their size chosen for you, and the Item Forge can install projectile-weapon upgrades. The Item Forge keeps one grade label per item, keeps a base's published grade, and says which requested upgrades did not fit. Mechanic and Technomancer have Standard presets, shops and hoards skip items with no price, and the windows have a calmer look.

ClassFixes.Title: Every class builds cleanly
ClassFixes.Body: Player characters of every class now build from level 1 to 20. Feat choices check the character's planned attributes and skill ranks at each level, so dedications and feats that need, for example, Charisma +2 appear when they are legal. General feat slots can also hold skill feats, as in the system. Operative specializations keep the feat they need. If no legal feat exists for a slot, the character is still created with that slot empty and the GM gets a whisper saying which slots to fill by hand.

TechCore.Title: Mechanic and Technomancer player characters
TechCore.Body: SimplySF2e now needs the Starfinder 2e system 1.6 or later. Player characters can be Mechanics or Technomancers from Tech Core. A Technomancer gets the magic hack that matches its programming language. A Mechanic who picks the Drone exocortex gets a reminder to set up the drone companion by hand.

UiRefresh.Title: Easier to read, more Starfinder
UiRefresh.Body: Small labels and table headings are larger, and input fields have clearer borders. After a preview appears, Create is the main button and Generate offers another version. Icons and Item Forge wording now fit Starfinder: a microchip for the Generator, gears for the Item Forge and a bolt for Generate.

CreatureArt.Title: Creature art keeps its token
CreatureArt.Body: With an art module installed, a generated creature now keeps the token art and scale of the similar bestiary creature it borrows from, instead of reusing its portrait. Its token is named after the new creature, and encounter copies are numbered in their token name too.

WhatsNew.Title: What's new
WhatsNew.Body: This window. It opens once after an update that changes something you can see. Reopen it any time with /sf2e whatsnew.

ReskinTrample.Title: Reskin keeps Trample in step
ReskinTrample.Body: When a Reskin renames a melee Strike, a Trample ability the module built for that creature now names the new Strike. Published creatures are not changed.

UiPolish.Title: Cleaner windows
UiPolish.Body: Previews fold the token report into one line, encounter cards show stats as a grid, the character review lists what to check, AI Provider Setup and Compendium Sources are easier to scan (with a pack filter), and narrow windows read better.

FasterEncounters.Title: Faster encounters
FasterEncounters.Body: Encounter mode builds several creatures at the same time, so big encounters are ready sooner.

Treasure.Title: Treasure hoards
Treasure.Body: A new Treasure window (Actors sidebar button or /sf2e treasure) fills one encounter's or a whole level's treasure budget with real Starfinder items and credits, and creates a loot actor.

Relevel.Title: Re-level a creature
Relevel.Body: In Reskin mode, set a new level. The copy's AC, HP, attacks, saves, skills and DCs move to the Starfinder GM Core values for that level, keeping how strong each stat was.

Errors.NetworkError: Could not reach the AI provider: {message}. Check the API Base URL and your internet connection. For a local or self-hosted provider, make sure it is running and allows requests from Foundry (CORS).
Errors.InvalidResponse: The AI provider sent back a reply the module could not read. Check that the API Base URL points to the provider's chat API, which usually ends in /v1.
Errors.EmptyResponse: The AI provider sent back an empty answer. Check the provider's status page and the model name, then try again.
Errors.ReasoningWithoutJson: The AI sent back reasoning text but no answer. Try again. If it keeps happening, choose a different model.
Errors.Truncated: The AI ran out of room before finishing its answer. Try again, use a shorter prompt, or choose a different model. Raise Max response tokens in Module Settings only if its value is below {max}.
Errors.RunBudgetExceeded: This run used its {limit}-token budget and stopped. To allow more, raise Run token budget in Module Settings → SimplySF2e (0 turns the limit off), then start a new run.
Errors.RunDeadline: This run passed its time limit and stopped. To allow more time, raise Run deadline (minutes) in Module Settings → SimplySF2e (0 turns the limit off), then start a new run.
Errors.Timeout: The AI provider sent no data for {seconds} seconds, so the request was stopped. Check the API Base URL and the provider's status. If the provider is slow, raise Request timeout (seconds) in Module Settings → SimplySF2e, then try again.
Errors.BadJson: The AI answer was in a format the module could not read. Try again. If it keeps failing, choose a different model.
Errors.BadStructure: The AI answer was incomplete ({detail}). Try again, or choose a more capable model.
Errors.NoBestiaryScaffold: No usable NPC actor was found in the enabled Bestiary Actors sources. Open Compendium Sources, enable a pack with NPC actors, then try again.
Errors.WrongSystem: SimplySF2e only works in a Starfinder 2e world. Open a world that uses the Starfinder Second Edition (sf2e) game system.

Shop.Title: SimplySF2e Shop
Shop.Prompt: What does it sell, and who runs it?
Shop.PromptPlaceholder: A cramped weapons stall on Absalom Station run by a retired soldier who only sells what she has field-tested.
Shop.SourcesDetail: Stock comes only from your equipment compendiums, at their published prices.
Shop.LevelHint: Stock is this level or lower.
Shop.NoEquipmentPack: No equipment compendium is enabled. Check Compendium Sources.
Shop.NoCandidates: No equipment of this level, type and rarity was found in your compendiums. Try a higher level or rarity.
Shop.NoStock: The AI picked nothing from the offered items. Generate again.
Shop.EmptyHint: Describe a shop and pick a level. The AI names it and chooses its stock from your sf2e equipment compendium; every item and price is the published one. Create makes a merchant you can drag onto a scene.
Shop.StockTotal: Total stock value: {total} credits. Prices are the compendium's own.
Shop.AllRemoved: Every item was removed. Generate again to restock.
Shop.Dropped: {count} pick(s) were not on the offered list and were left out.

Relevel.Label: New level
Relevel.Hint: Change it to re-level the copy. Each number keeps its Starfinder GM Core scale (high, moderate and so on) at the new level.
Relevel.UnchangedSummary: What else moves, and what stays
Relevel.Unchanged: Area blasts, auras and filled glossary abilities the module built are rebuilt for the new level. Published abilities keep their text. Spells and their ranks, the ritual DC, gear, and Elite/Weak stay as they are. Attributes and skills also move, and very low ones (below every GM Core scale) stay put.
Relevel.Notice: The copy is moved to level {level} with the GM Core tables. Rules, traits, spells, and items are copied unchanged. The original creature is not modified.

Treasure.Title: SimplySF2e Treasure
Treasure.PartyHint: Party size only shows an "each" figure. The budget is per party, so it does not change.
Treasure.PromptPlaceholder: Abandoned corporate lab on an ice moon
Treasure.SourcesDetail: Items come only from your equipment compendiums, at their published prices.
Treasure.NoEquipmentPack: No equipment compendium is enabled. Check Compendium Sources.
Treasure.NoCandidates: No equipment of this level and rarity was found in your compendiums. Try a higher level or rarity.
Treasure.NoItems: Nothing fit the budget. Generate again.
Treasure.EmptyHint: Set the party level and how much to give out. The module sets the budget from the Starfinder GM Core Treasure by Level table; the AI themes the hoard and picks real items from your sf2e equipment compendium, and the rest is paid out as credits. Create makes a loot actor.
Treasure.AllRemoved: Every item was removed. The whole budget is now credits.
Treasure.Dropped: {count} pick(s) were not offered, had no price, or did not fit the budget, and were left out.

StatCheck.Heading: Stat check
StatCheck.AllOk: {name}: all {total} numbers match the preview and sit inside the GM Core range for level {level}.
StatCheck.RowDiffers: {label} {actual} on the sheet, but the preview said {expected}
StatCheck.RowUnreadable: {label}: could not be read from the sheet
StatCheck.BandAbove: above the GM Core extreme benchmark
StatCheck.BandBelow: below the lowest GM Core benchmark
StatCheck.ChatIntro: SimplySF2e stat check found numbers to review. Nothing on the actor was changed.
StatCheck.Failed: The stat check could not run; the actor was created normally.
